messages:
Priya (Product): Quick check: proposing keyboard shortcuts for the scorecard list to speed up QA flows. Sketch: focus list -> use j/k to move rows, space to expand diff, A to approve selected, shift+A for bulk approve. Thoughts?

Ethan (Design): Love the keyboard-first idea. Two UX notes: 1) include a visible key hint (small pill) when the list is focused; 2) avoid mapping single-letter keys that conflict with browser shortcuts. Maybe use upper-case (Shift+A) for destructive actions.

Raj (Engineering): Technical: we can implement j/k and space easily. For A/Shift+A we should require a confirmation modal for bulk approve. Also need to ensure these don't trigger when an input is focused (search box / inline edit).

Mei (Research): From observed workflows, power users will appreciate a command palette as well (Cmd+K -> type "approve"), but discoverability is key for occasional users. Key hint + a small "Keyboard shortcuts" help link in the header would cover both.

Jules (Accessibility): A11y checklist for keyboard features:
- Ensure all actions have aria-keyshortcuts attributes (e.g., aria-keyshortcuts="j k" on the list container).
- Manage focus order: when diff expands, focus should move into the diff region and pressing Escape should collapse and return focus to the row.
- Announce changes to screen readers: use live region to announce "Diff opened for Prompt set: <name>" and "1 of 4 diffs" when paging.
- Avoid relying on case-sensitive shortcuts; assistive tech may not map Shift consistently. Consider modifier combos (e.g., Alt+Enter) as fallback.

Priya (Product): Good call on confirmation for bulk approve. Copy dilemma: modal header options: "Approve 12 prompt tests" vs "Confirm approval" vs "Approve for rollout". Which is clearest?

Ethan (Design): "Approve 12 prompt tests" is explicit and shows count. Add a short subtext: "This will mark the selected tests as approved for rollout." Keep primary button: "Approve" (brand-safe, short). Secondary: "Cancel".

Jules (Accessibility): For the modal, ensure the primary action is focused by default but also provide a clear accessible description: aria-describedby points to the subtext. Also include an aria-alert after success: "12 tests approved".

Raj (Engineering): Backend note: approve endpoint returns job id; sometimes processing can take a few seconds for large batches. Suggest UI show a progress toast "Approvals processing (12)" and disable further approve actions until job completes or show per-row pending state. That will prevent duplicate submits.

QA-bot: Regression test suggestions:
- Shortcut focus: confirm j/k cycle through visible rows only (not hidden rows in virtual list)
- Space toggles diff expansion and trap focus within diff until Escape
- A (single) triggers modal with accurate count, Shift+A triggers bulk modal with list preview
- Keyboard shortcuts are disabled when inline edit or search input is focused
- Live region announcements occur on open/close
I'll create a checklist and link to the test run.

Mei (Research): Small UX experiment: A/B test two flows for 2 weeks: Variant A shows sticky key hint + command palette, Variant B shows just a one-time tooltip to learn shortcuts. Measure task completion time and adoption.

Priya (Product): Agreed. Action items:
- Ethan: mock modal copy + key hint UI + command palette entry (Figma link) (due Wed).
- Raj: implement keyboard handlers with input-focus guard and backend idempotency for approve endpoint (PR by next Fri).
- Jules: provide exact ARIA attributes and live region copy (by Tue).
- QA-bot / Nora: add regression tests and a short automation plan (by Thu).
- Mei: draft A/B test plan and metrics (by Mon).

Ethan (Design): One more micro copy thing: toast text after approval  avoid "Done". Prefer "12 tests approved" and include an undo link for 10s.

Raj (Engineering): Undo will be a soft state toggle that calls a revert endpoint with the approval job id. We'll add 10s client-side undo and a server-side revert API.

Jules (Accessibility): Ensure the undo link is keyboard-focusable and announced as "Undo approval" by screen readers.

Priya (Product): Perfect. I'll spin up a ticket and drop the Figma link + acceptance criteria. Thanks all :rocket:
